common_name: Woodard Rabbiteye Blueberry (Classic Large-Berried Southern Blueberry)

planting.note: Plant in late winter to early spring in acidic, well-drained soil in full sun; Woodard needs a compatible rabbiteye pollinator such as Climax or Tifblue nearby for good fruit set.

directions: Plant in acidic (pH 4.5-5.5), well-drained soil amended with pine bark in full sun with a compatible pollinator variety nearby. One of the older, longer-established rabbiteye blueberry cultivars, Woodard is valued for its unusually large, soft-textured, mild-flavored berries that ripen in early-to-mid season, a bit ahead of many later rabbiteye types. The bushes are moderately vigorous and productive, though the soft fruit texture makes it better suited to fresh home use and processing than commercial shipping. Keep soil consistently moist through bloom and fruit development, and mulch well to conserve moisture and maintain the acidic soil conditions blueberries require.

common_name: Pride of Houston Yaupon Holly (Upright Berry-Producing Native Holly)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter, spring, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Pride of Houston is an upright, female selection of native yaupon holly that sets heavy crops of red berries and can be grown as a large shrub or limbed into a small multi-trunked tree.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun to partial shade. Pride of Houston is an upright, densely branched selection of native yaupon holly that, unlike the compact dwarf yaupon forms, is a female clone that produces abundant bright red berries prized for winter interest and wildlife value, holding well into the colder months. It grows into a substantial large shrub or can be pruned up into a small evergreen tree for use as a screen or specimen, and like all yaupon selections it is extremely tolerant of heat, drought, wind, salt spray, and poor soil, making it one of the toughest Gulf Coast landscape plants available. It needs only occasional shaping and no supplemental water once established.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun for best golden color; Sunshine Ligustrum is a sterile, non-fruiting sport selected specifically to avoid the invasive seeding of common Chinese privet.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun, where the foliage colors most brightly; in shadier sites the leaves stay more chartreuse-green than gold. Sunshine Ligustrum was selected as a sterile, non-flowering, non-fruiting sport of common Chinese privet specifically to provide the same tough, brightly colored foliage without the invasive seeding that has made the wild species a serious problem in Southern woodlands. Because it never flowers or sets berries, it channels its energy into dense, compact growth and vivid golden-yellow foliage color that holds through the heat of summer, making it a popular low hedge, mass planting, or color accent shrub. It tolerates heat, drought, and poor soil with ease and needs only occasional shearing to maintain a tidy shape.

common_name: Majestic Beauty Indian Hawthorn (Tree-Form Large Indian Hawthorn)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring, summer, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Majestic Beauty grows considerably larger than standard Indian hawthorn and can be trained as a small multi-trunked tree or large screening shrub.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun. Majestic Beauty is a hybrid Indian hawthorn selected for its unusually large mature size, growing into a substantial large shrub or small tree rather than the compact rounded mound typical of most Indian hawthorn cultivars, which makes it useful for screening, specimen planting, or a small flowering tree in coastal landscapes. In spring it produces abundant clusters of fragrant, light pink flowers followed by small blue-black berries that attract birds, all on glossy, leathery, disease-resistant foliage. It shares the species' outstanding tolerance for salt spray, wind, and poor sandy soils, making it a strong performer in exposed coastal Gulf sites, though good air circulation helps minimize the leaf spot disease that can affect Indian hawthorn in humid conditions.

common_name: Eleanor Taber Indian Hawthorn (Deep Pink-Flowered Indian Hawthorn)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring, summer, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Eleanor Taber is valued for its deep rose-pink flowers, showier than the paler pink or white of many Indian hawthorn selections.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun for the heaviest bloom, though it tolerates partial shade with somewhat reduced flowering. Eleanor Taber is a long-popular Indian hawthorn selection prized for its especially deep, rich rose-pink flower clusters in spring, a stronger color than the softer pinks and whites typical of the species, set against the same leathery, dark green, disease-resistant foliage. Like other Indian hawthorn selections it is outstanding for coastal Gulf landscapes, tolerating salt spray, wind, and poor sandy soil with ease, and needs only a light shaping prune right after spring bloom to keep its naturally tidy, rounded form. Good air circulation helps reduce Entomosporium leaf spot, the main disease concern for Indian hawthorn in humid climates.
